title: De novo myasthenia gravis in a patient with malignant melanoma after concurrent SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: Case report and literature review
case_prompt: A 65-year-old woman with metastatic melanoma presented three weeks after her second pembrolizumab infusion and second dose of the BBIBP-CorV COVID-19 vaccine with a two-day history of bilateral diplopia and ptosis that worsened as the day progressed. She had received her first pembrolizumab infusion and first BBIBP-CorV dose without incident. On examination, there was bilateral ocular weakness without limb weakness. Brain MRI showed no evidence of metastases, and repeat neck MRI demonstrated significant reduction in the size of her known cervical soft-tissue mass. Laboratory testing revealed a creatine kinase (CK) level of 4704 U/L (normal 26–192 U/L) and an aldolase level of 98.6 U/L (normal 1.0–7.5 U/L). Transthoracic echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 57 %, and the CK-MB to total CK ratio was 4 %. Electromyography demonstrated notable decremental changes in the compound muscle action potentials during repetitive nerve stimulation at low rates of 2–4 Hz.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Myasthenia gravis considered — “The electromyography … showed notable decremental changes … characteristic of MG.”  
2. Myositis considered — “While elevated CK levels are atypical for MG, this finding raised a differential consideration for accompanying myositis …”  
3. Myocarditis excluded — “Myocardial involvement was considered less likely due to a preserved ejection fraction of 57 % … and a CK-MB to total CK ratio of less than 6 % …”  
4. Inflammatory myopathies or rhabdomyolysis considered — “Other conditions associated with immune activation, such as inflammatory myopathies or rhabdomyolysis, can result in elevated CK and should be considered in the differential.”
